subject: Architecture
title: The I-35W Mississippi Bridge: Wake-Up Call
description: A 60-second lesson on The I-35W Mississippi Bridge: Wake-Up Call.

hook.text: On August 1, 2007, a busy Minneapolis highway bridge collapsed during rush hour, killing 13 people.

buildup.text: The I-35W bridge had been rated 'structurally deficient' for 17 years before it failed.

discovery.text: Gusset plates — thin steel connectors — were half as thick as they should have been. A design error from 1967.

twist.text: Heavy construction equipment on the deck at the time of collapse added extra load to already weak connections.

climax.text: The U.S. government allocated $1.7 billion for bridge repairs. Over 70,000 bridges were still rated deficient.

punchline.text: We knew it was failing. We just didn't fix it in time.

quiz.question: What design flaw caused the I-35W bridge collapse?
options: The foundations were built on unstable sand
Gusset plates were half as thick as they should have been
The suspension cables corroded from road salt
